editorial:
Imagine trying to plan the perfect engagement party while your mothers are basically at war. That is exactly what you get with Riley and Mandla. You will feel for this couple as they try to balance their love with the huge amount of pressure coming from their families. The vibe is cozy and romantic, making it the kind of movie you put on when you just want to relax and feel good. It captures that stressful but funny feeling of trying to please everyone during the holidays, and the chemistry between the leads makes you really root for them to make it work.

What really works here is how the movie handles the family drama without getting too heavy. The acting feels natural, and the pacing keeps you interested even when the arguments get repetitive. While it follows some predictable romance tropes, the big royal surprise adds a nice layer of tension.
endingExplained: After all the fighting, the couple finally confronts the royal secret that threatened to pull them apart. They decide that their love is more important than family expectations or royal titles. The movie wraps up with a heartfelt engagement party where the two mothers finally stop arguing and accept each other. You see Riley and Mandla commit to their future together, proving that they can handle any surprise as long as they stay a team.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves royal romances and family drama.
